subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Voyager's Grand Tour
description: A short lesson to help you apply Voyager's Grand Tour.

hook.text: In 1977, Voyager 1 and 2 launched to visit the giant planets. Both still send signals from interstellar space.

buildup.text: A rare alignment let one probe slingshot from planet to planet. Such alignment occurs once every 176 years.

discovery.text: Voyager found volcanoes on Io, geysers on Triton, and signs of a hidden ocean beneath Europa's ice.

twist.text: Each carries a Golden Record—music, greetings in 55 languages, and images of Earth for any finder.

climax.text: Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012—the farthest human-made object, over 24 billion km away.

punchline.text: Launched in 1977, still calling home. The farthest hello.

quiz.question: What is special about the Golden Record carried by each Voyager probe?
options: It contains music, images, and greetings intended for any alien civilization that finds it
It stores scientific data collected during the mission
It plays a recording of mission control communications

details.summary: Launched in 1977, Voyagers 1 and 2 exploited a rare planetary alignment to visit Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune — the 'Grand Tour.' They discovered active volcanoes on Io, rings around Jupiter, and Neptune's Great Dark Spot.
details.whyItMatters: The Voyager missions are humanity's greatest exploration achievement — the first spacecraft to visit all four giant planets and the first human-made objects to leave the solar system.
takeaways: Voyagers exploited a rare alignment to visit all four giant planets
They discovered volcanism on Io and rings around Jupiter
Both are in interstellar space, still transmitting after 47 years

faq.question: How far away are the Voyagers now?
faq.answer: Voyager 1 is over 24 billion kilometers from Earth — the most distant human-made object. Voyager 2 is about 20 billion kilometers away. Both crossed the heliopause (the boundary of the Sun's influence) and are in interstellar space. Radio signals take over 22 hours to reach Voyager 1.

faq.question: How long will the Voyagers continue to function?
faq.answer: Their plutonium-238 power sources decay by about 4 watts per year. By the mid-2030s, there won't be enough power for any instruments. After that, they'll drift silently through the galaxy for millions of years. In about 40,000 years, Voyager 1 will pass within 1.6 light-years of the star Gliese 445.
